question.text: Ms. Neha Raghavan, Head of IR at Saraswati Capital AIF, is drafting a Benchmarking Note for LPs and needs to articulate the primary function of a market index in modern investment management. Which of the following statements BEST captures what an index is and what it does in the AIF context?

answer.text: An index is a predictive model that forecasts future market returns based on GDP trends and interest rate expectations.
An index is a regulatory construct mandated by SEBI for computing the fair value of unlisted equity positions held by Category I AIFs.

An index is a composite measure that reflects the change in value of an underlying basket of securities from a base value, used as a gauge of the market, a benchmark for active managers, and the underlying portfolio for passive funds.
An index is solely a price-weighted arithmetic average of constituent securities, designed to track short-term trader sentiment on listed instruments.

explanation.text: The Logic: An index is a composite measure that reflects the change in the value of underlying securities over time relative to a base value. Its documented uses are: (i) a gauge of market performance, (ii) a benchmark for actively managed portfolios, (iii) the underlying portfolio for passive index funds, and (iv) the proxy for the market portfolio of risky assets in CAPM for measuring systematic risk. The Trap: Option A confuses an index (a descriptive measure) with a forecasting model. Option B is false — SEBI does not mandate an index for AIF valuation. Option D limits indices to price-weighted only, ignoring value-weighted, equal-weighted, and fundamental-weighted variants. Note: All four documented uses share the same underlying construct — a composite measure tracking change from a base value.
